The two-way ranging functionality is based on sequences that can be e.g. Pseudo-Noise (PN) ranging (phase modulated together with the TC/TM data, and turned around either transparently (bent pipe) or regeneratively), or using Spread Quadrature Pseudo Noise. Space missions could benefit in increased accuracy and onboard autonomy from a timestamping function. It is based on a one Pulse-Per-Second (1 PPS) signal and time information generated by the transponder based on the PN ranging epoch combined with known range information and other information from ground segment, thus implementing one-way time transfer from earth.The implementation involves the TTC receiver locking to the PN uplink sequence and generating regular epoch. The ground station is performing 2-way ranging usingthe PN-ranging signals, including removal of ambiguity and other processing on the orbit. This information including ranging/range-rate from the ground station is then uplinked to the TTC receiver via telecommand. The receiver then performs a Timing algorithm and dynamic model, to generate onboard time using the received epoch timing and the information uplinked from the ground station.
